column1: # Fail-closed build guard map for the baked worker toolchain.
# One row per package in the sibling devbox.json, TAB-separated:
#     <devbox package>  <binary to resolve, or - >  <smoke command, or - >
# assert-toolchain.sh cross-checks column 1 against what `devbox global install`
# ACTUALLY installed, so this file cannot silently fall behind devbox.json: adding a
# package there without adding a row here FAILS THE BUILD, which is the whole point.
# That drift is not hypothetical -- it is why this file exists. The guard it replaces
# was a hardcoded `command -v python3 && ... && command -v openssl` line that stopped
# tracking the manifest, and by 0.11.11 five baked packages (file, perl, coreutils,
# kubernetes-helm, kubeconform) had no coverage at all while CI stayed green.
# Column 2 is `-` when a package legitimately ships NO binary in the profile. Do not
# guess this column: MEASURE it against a built image. `fontconfig` is the trap --
# it sounds like it brings `fc-cache`/`fc-list` and it does not (both measured
# MISSING on /opt/uzi-toolchain/bin, 2026-07-27), which is exactly why the
# font-cache warm at the bottom of each Dockerfile wraps `fc-cache` in a
# `command -v` conditional. A guard that assumed the binary would fail every build.
# Column 3 runs the tool rather than merely resolving it, because resolving proves a
# symlink exists and nothing more. The openssl.bin lesson (see devbox.json) is the
# reason: a package can land its libs and man pages while the CLI never appears.
# `-` when there is no cheap non-interactive smoke, or when a later, better guard
# already covers it -- chromium is smoke-tested properly by the `--dump-dom` guard
# further down each Dockerfile, so duplicating a weaker check here would buy nothing.
